# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)

<!-- Generated by `omni docs build` (REQ-060) for OmniEngineering Workspace. Do not edit; regenerate. -->

Related assistant workflow: [clarify](../../.claude/skills/clarify/SKILL.md) to capture new requirements before they land here.

What OmniEngineering Workspace must do. One row per requirement in `.ai/requirements/requirements.json`, grouped by area: its status, priority, how many tests are linked to it, and the first sentence of its description. Acceptance criteria follow for the requirements that are still open.

Which tests and files belong to each requirement is in the [Requirements Traceability Matrix](requirements-traceability.md); the validation each one asks for is in the [Test Plan and Coverage Summary](test-plan.md). For a single requirement in full run `omni requirement show <id>`; `omni docs build --detail full` writes every requirement in full here. Change requirements with `omni requirement add|update|complete`, never here.

| REQ-013 | Add omni update: 3-way-merge template improvements into adopted workspaces | completed | high | 0 | The single biggest 'clunky' gap raised this session: once a project adopts OmniEngineering and customizes its rules/playbooks/checklists, there was no way to pull later template improvements in except a manual hand-diff-and-port (done twice by hand earlier this session). (more: `omni requirement show REQ-013`) |
| REQ-014 | Fix: omni update must not re-run sync when make_ai.py itself has an unresolved conflict | completed | medium | 0 | Found live while dogfooding REQ-013 against STEP_App's genuinely diverged make_ai.py: when make_ai.py's own merge produced a conflict, the file was written with unresolved <<<<<<< markers (correct), but run_update still treated that as make_ai.py having 'changed' and re-ran sync in a fresh subprocess against the now-syntactically-invalid file, producing a raw Python SyntaxError traceback instead of a clean message. (more: `omni requirement show REQ-014`) |
| REQ-017 | Fix: adopting or updating omni_graph.py must not be able to break every other command | completed | high | 0 | Found by end-to-end testing REQ-015 against a simulated pre-existing application: (1) ADOPTION_CLI_FILES only listed omni/make_ai.py, so `omni adopt --include-cli` copied a make_ai.py that unconditionally imports omni_graph without ever copying omni_graph.py itself, crashing every single omni command (not just `graph`) in the adopted project with a raw ModuleNotFoundError. (more: `omni requirement show REQ-017`) |
| REQ-042 | Arbiter version tracking and omni arbiter update | completed | medium | 1 | omni update never touched an installed or vendored Arbiter. arbiter_install records {source, version} under arbiter in .ai/omni-version.json (other keys preserved); doctor warns when the installed version differs; omni update warns when the installed completion.arbiter_gate rule drifted from the template; omni arbiter update [--source] [--keep-rule] [--squash] [--force] upgrades the package, rewrites the rule, pulls the subtree when one is vendored (refusing to mix squash modes unless forced), re-records the version and suggests a baseline refresh. |
| REQ-044 | Requirement id aliases and omni requirement renumber | completed | high | 1 | Two workspaces that both use the REQ prefix collide the moment one is vendored into the other. The registry gains an optional id_aliases map (old id to new id). (more: `omni requirement show REQ-044`) |
| REQ-049 | omni arbiter sync levels the subtree, the installed package, the recorded version and the baseline in one command; doctor warns on a mismatched commit identity | completed | high | 2 | The three-way sync (subtree pull, pip install, version record, baseline refresh, doctor) was manual and error-prone. omni arbiter sync runs the steps in order and stops at the first failure naming the step; --dry-run prints the commands; in pip mode it updates and re-baselines. (more: `omni requirement show REQ-049`) |

## Acceptance criteria of open requirements

No requirement is open.
